text.tspan: Response to reviews of manuscript #GSAB-B39345 "Continental
megathrust earthquake potential partition coupled with the
geological mountain-building sequences in the great Nepal
Himalaya"

svg.text: Huai Zhang, Zhen Zhang, Lin Ding, Guangyao Yin, Yicun Guo, Yuanze Zhou, Yaolin Shi

text.tspan: We greatly appreciate the Editor and reviewers for their insightful comments and
suggestions. We have carefully revised the manuscript and provide a point-by-point
response below.
(1) The assumption of a spatially stable interseismic coupling pattern over the
entire Cenozoic provides a reasonable first-order simplification. It would be
helpful if the authors could briefly acknowledge this assumption and clarify its
limitations in the manuscript.
We thank the reviewer for this constructive suggestion. We agree that the
assumption of a spatially stable interseismic coupling pattern should be
stated more explicitly. In the revised manuscript, we have clarified that
the binary locked-creeping pattern is used as a first-order approximation
based on the present-day geodetic coupling pattern and the flat-ramp-flat
geometry of the MHT.
To perform the mapping projection, we assume that the first-order locked-creeping
segmentation of the MHT has remained spatially stable during the main Cenozoic
evolution of the Nepal Himalayan wedge. Nevertheless, this treatment is a first-
order simplification. Long-term changes in fault geometry, thermal structure,
erosion, or regional tectonic configuration may have modified the exact position
and width of the coupling transition through time.
(2) The connection between the model results and present-day deformation could be
slightly strengthened by comparing the results with general patterns from existing
geodetic observations.
We appreciate this helpful suggestion. We have added a qualitative
comparison with GPS-derived interseismic coupling patterns along the MHT.
